readme:
# TD-MPC2 单纯形潜变量与精英轨迹更新

## 1. 问题

TD-MPC2 单纯形潜变量与精英轨迹更新：实现下列接口并通过数值、边界和实验检查。

提取SimNorm与MPPI已选精英的加权矩更新；候选轨迹与价值作为输入，不学习动力学/Q网络或执行真实MPC。

## 2. 核心公式

$$
z_{g,:}=\operatorname{softmax}(x_{g,:}),\quad w_i=\operatorname{softmax}(\tau Q_i),\quad\mu=\sum_iw_i a_i,\quad\sigma=\operatorname{clip}(\sqrt{\sum_iw_i(a_i-\mu)^2},\sigma_{min},\sigma_{max}).
$$

## 3. 公式到代码

- `simnorm(values: Tensor, group_dim: int) -> Tensor`
- `elite_moments(actions: Tensor, values: Tensor, temperature: float, min_std: float, max_std: float) -> tuple`

SimNorm在每个小组内归一化，不能让整个latent共享一个softmax。轨迹权重沿精英E维，对整条时域共享。官方temperature乘价值；方差围绕加权均值，最后再夹标准差。公式用精确归一化，省略源码分母的1e-9数值保护。

## 4. 本题约定

simnorm输入任意rank>=1浮点张量，末维被group_dim整除且group_dim>=2。actions为(H,E,D)，values为(E,)，temperature>=0且为乘数；0<min_std<=max_std。返回(H,D)的mean/std。

校验辅助函数已提供。浮点输入为有限 CPU float32/float64，不修改输入；非法形状、类型、范围或掩码必须抛出 `ValueError`。

## 5. 交互图与确定性实验

`experiment.py` 在固定输入上调用提交的全部接口，记录学习或采样曲线与末端指标。实验逻辑和阈值见 T3，输出同样用于可视化。

可视化由 `viz/gen.py` 生成；T3 将你的函数传入同一实验并记录真实指标。这是小规模确定性教学实验，不是机器人基准成绩。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 来源与延伸

- [TD-MPC2: Scalable, Robust World Models for Continuous Control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.16828) — SimNorm and official _plan elite weighted mean/std update
- [Verified source](https://github.com/nicklashansen/tdmpc2/blob/main/tdmpc2/common/layers.py)
- [Verified source](https://github.com/nicklashansen/tdmpc2/blob/main/tdmpc2/tdmpc2.py)

核验日期：2026-10-28。扩展到完整论文系统还需要本题范围中明确省略的模型、数据和环境。

## 测试捕获的错误

- Temperature divides elite values instead of multiplying them.
- Second moment is mistaken for centered variance.

## 实验范围

## 可重复实验记录

2步1维动作、25点二维网格，选择8精英，12轮更新；temperature=5，std范围[0.03,1]。初始均值0，要求终误差<初始3%；另检查两个3维单纯形质量和。

判题固定seed=42。计算采用CPU float64、显式输入，涉及优化时使用普通梯度更新；不下载数据集或模型权重。原生PyTorch与真实Pyodide/NumPy-WASM执行同一套T0–T3测试。阈值针对本教学实验。

# TD-MPC2 Simplex Latents and Elite Trajectory Updates

## 1. Exercise goal

TD-MPC2 Simplex Latents and Elite Trajectory Updates: implement the interfaces below and verify numerical, boundary and experimental behavior.

Isolate SimNorm and MPPI weighted moments for already-selected elites. Candidate trajectories and values are supplied; omit learned dynamics/Q networks and real MPC.

## 2. Core equations

$$
z_{g,:}=\operatorname{softmax}(x_{g,:}),\quad w_i=\operatorname{softmax}(\tau Q_i),\quad\mu=\sum_iw_i a_i,\quad\sigma=\operatorname{clip}(\sqrt{\sum_iw_i(a_i-\mu)^2},\sigma_{min},\sigma_{max}).
$$

## 3. From equations to code

- `simnorm(values: Tensor, group_dim: int) -> Tensor`
- `elite_moments(actions: Tensor, values: Tensor, temperature: float, min_std: float, max_std: float) -> tuple`

SimNorm normalizes each group separately. Elite weights normalize E and are shared across the trajectory horizon. Official temperature multiplies values; compute variance around the weighted mean and clamp standard deviation afterward. Use exact normalization, omitting the source denominator epsilon 1e-9.

## 4. Contract and boundaries

Simnorm accepts rank>=1 floating inputs with last dimension divisible by group_dim>=2. Actions are (H,E,D), values (E,), temperature>=0 is a multiplier, 0<min_std<=max_std. Return mean/std of shape (H,D).

Validation helpers are provided. All floating inputs are finite CPU float32/float64; do not mutate inputs. Invalid shape, dtype, range or mask arguments raise `ValueError`.

## 5. Deterministic experiment and visualization

`experiment.py` calls every submitted interface on fixed inputs and records a learning or sampling curve and terminal metrics. T3 states the behavioral thresholds; the visualization uses the same outputs.

The visualization is generated by `viz/gen.py`; T3 runs the same experiment with your functions and records its actual metrics. These are small deterministic teaching results, not a robot benchmark.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Sources and extensions

- [TD-MPC2: Scalable, Robust World Models for Continuous Control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.16828) — SimNorm and official _plan elite weighted mean/std update
- [Verified source](https://github.com/nicklashansen/tdmpc2/blob/main/tdmpc2/common/layers.py)
- [Verified source](https://github.com/nicklashansen/tdmpc2/blob/main/tdmpc2/tdmpc2.py)

Verified 2026-10-28. Extending this operator to the full paper requires the omitted model, data and environment described in the scope above.

## Mistakes caught by the tests

- Temperature divides elite values instead of multiplying them.
- Second moment is mistaken for centered variance.

## Experimental scope

Isolate SimNorm and MPPI weighted moments for already-selected elites. Candidate trajectories and values are supplied; omit learned dynamics/Q networks and real MPC.

Two-step scalar actions, a 25-point two-dimensional grid, eight elites and twelve updates; temperature 5, std range [.03,1]. Start at zero mean and require final error below 3% of initial; also check mass sums of two three-dimensional simplexes.
